title: Article 345 — Official language or languages of a State

content.overview: Article 345 provides that subject to Articles 346 and 347, the Legislature of a State may by law adopt any one or more of the languages in use in the State or Hindi as the language or languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of that State. Until the Legislature of the State otherwise provides by law, English shall continue to be used for those official purposes within the State for which it was being used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution.
content.glance: State Legislature may adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, for official purposes of the State. English continues until the State by law otherwise provides.
content.study:
Article 345 State official language:
- State Legislature may by law adopt any one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, for official purposes of the State.
- Subject to Arts 346 (Union–State communication) and 347 (special provision for language spoken by a section of the population).
- English continues for pre-commencement official purposes until the State Legislature otherwise provides.

Examination: State choice; languages in use or Hindi; English interim; link 346–347.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: State Legislature may by law adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, for official purposes of the State. English continues until the State otherwise provides by law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is the official language of a State determined under Article 345?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 345, subject to Articles 346 and 347, the Legislature of a State may by law adopt any one or more of the languages in use in the State or Hindi as the language or languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of that State. Until the State Legislature otherwise provides by law, English continues to be used for those official purposes within the State for which it was used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution.
